raw_response:
I'm 73 this year, and these 3 mu of land in Quzhou I've been working for 40 years. My back isn't what it used to be, and my knees ache when it rains. My son and his wife both work in the factory over in the county town — they send back a bit of money when they can, but I can't count on it. It's mostly me and my wife doing the farming now. My daughter-in-law helped during harvest last year, but she's busy with her own job. We don't hire labor — can't afford it. Every yuan that goes into the field is a yuan we don't have for medicine or for when the grandkids visit.

**Wheat**

I'll plant the wheat around October 12th, same as I always do. If you plant too early, the wheat grows too tall before winter and freezes; too late, and it doesn't establish right. I know this land. I'm using the same seed as last year — saved some from the harvest, cleaned it myself. No need to buy new seed for wheat, it's not like corn. That saves me maybe 30 yuan per mu.

For fertilizer, last year I used about one bag of compound fertilizer (复合肥) for the whole field at planting — that's around 25 jin per mu. My neighbor Lao Wang used a bit more and his yield was better, maybe 50 jin more per mu. So this year I'll put down a bag and a half total, about 40 jin per mu. Better to use a bit more than to risk a bad crop. I can't afford to lose yield — this wheat is half our grain for the year. Then in March, when the wheat is at jointing, I'll topdress with urea. I'll use almost two bags total, about 30 jin per mu. If the wheat looks yellow, I might add a bit more. I'd rather waste a little fertilizer than have thin grain.

I'll irrigate twice — once at planting if the soil is dry, and once at jointing in spring. Well water costs electricity, and every time I pump it's maybe 40 yuan. Three times would be better, but I need to keep some cash for the maize season. Twice is enough if it rains a bit in spring. Last year I did twice and got about 420 jin per mu. I'll hope for the same.

I'll spray herbicide once after planting — the weeds are bad if you don't. No insecticide for wheat usually, unless I see aphids.

Tillage? I hire Old Zhang's small tractor to rotary till (旋耕) once before planting. Costs me 80 yuan for the whole plot. I used to plow deep, but I'm too old for that now, and the tractor is fine.

**Maize**

Wheat harvest is early June, and you can't waste a single day — the maize has to go in right after. I'll buy hybrid seed from the supply shop. It's expensive, maybe 45 yuan per mu, but you have to. Saved seed doesn't work for maize anymore. 

For fertilizer, one bag of compound fertilizer at planting — about 20 jin per mu. Then when the corn is at the big trumpet stage (大喇叭口), I'll topdress with urea, about 25 jin per mu. That's less than the wheat because maize grows in summer when it's hot and the rain helps some. Last year I used too much and it lodged a bit in the wind. 

I'll irrigate once, maybe twice if July is dry. Usually the summer rains come, so once is enough most years. Costs less than wheat season.

For pesticides, I'll spray herbicide once, and insecticide if I see armyworms. Last year there were some bugs in August, so I'll keep an eye out. Maybe one spray.

Minimal tillage for maize — no time between harvest and planting anyway. Sometimes I just plant right into the wheat stubble if the field isn't too messy.

**Labor**

Family does it all. About 12 days for wheat season, 10 days for maize. Mostly me and my wife. During harvest, if my son can get leave, he comes back for two days. Otherwise we manage. Hired labor? No, can't afford 150 yuan per day.

**Costs**

Total cash I need to put in: seed, fertilizer, fuel for irrigation, pesticide, tractor hire. I figure about 1,300 yuan for the year. That's a lot for us. The wheat seed I saved helps. My son sent 2,000 yuan last month, so I have enough, but I need to keep some aside. If I spend everything on inputs and then someone gets sick, we're in trouble. That's why I don't irrigate three times — I need a buffer.

I expect about 420 kg per mu for wheat, maybe 450 kg per mu for maize. If prices are like last year, that should keep us fed and maybe sell a bit. Not much, but enough.
